plain: Plato's Republic ends with the story of Er, a soldier who dies in battle and comes back to tell what he saw after death. Two guests bring it up, both summarising Plato without other sources. The researcher Diana Pasulka calls it a recorded near-death experience, "about the soldier who dies in battle and has a near-death experience." The researcher James Madden tells it on another episode as Plato's story of a virtuous man: "Er was a virtuous person. He dies in battle for the city." Madden does not call it a near-death experience. Plato's text is the document both name. Whether it is an old memory of something like modern near-death accounts is the guests' reading, since the shape of the story is what they compare. If it is, people have been reporting the same journey past death for thousands of years.
